new guideline (Three generated tasks (P3, P4, P5) carry timing phrases in their labels ('in good time', 'within three days', 'immediately'), which pulls their labels away from the reference wording of the action itself. The retrieved documented and learned guidelines cover task type, merging and report cycles, but none says how to keep timing qualifiers out of task labels. A text annotation keeps the deadline in)

rules_sent_back.instruction: When the description makes a notification of an occurrence to one party conditional on whether the same occurrence has already been communicated to another party, and separately states that a notification of that occurrence must still be sent to a different party regardless of that earlier communication: Model an exclusive gateway before the conditional notification task, with one labeled outgoing sequence flow for the case where the earlier communication was made and one for the case where it was not. Route only the case the description makes conditional into the notification task. Model any notification the description requires regardless of the earlier communication as its own task on a path that is not controlled by that gateway, so it is never skipped. Do not nest the unconditional notification inside the branch of the conditional one.
rules_sent_back.situation: the description makes a notification of an occurrence to one party conditional on whether the same occurrence has already been communicated to another party, and separately states that a notification of that occurrence must still be sent to a different party regardless of that earlier communication

rules_sent_back.instruction: When the description states that a party must notify an external body about an event only when two conditions hold in sequence, such as a severity condition on the event and a check that no other party has already made the same notification, and the notification must not happen otherwise: Model each condition as its own exclusive gateway, placed in the order the description states them. Place the notification as its own task only on the path where every condition holds, and keep it separate from other steps rather than merging it into a gateway or another task. Route the paths where any condition fails past the notification. Merge all paths with an exclusive gateway before the process continues.
rules_sent_back.situation: the description states that a party must notify an external body about an event only when two conditions hold in sequence, such as a severity condition on the event and a check that no other party has already made the same notification, and the notification must not happen otherwise

rules_sent_back.instruction: When the description states a condition that decides whether the process continues to a further outcome or ends, for example 'if all criteria are met, ...' followed by a consequence: Model an exclusive gateway at the point where the condition is decided, with one labeled outgoing sequence flow for each outcome the description states. Place the gateway before the outcome that the condition governs, and do not leave the conditional outcome as an unconditional sequence of tasks.
rules_sent_back.situation: the description makes a report to a named body apply only when a stated condition holds, and that condition is whether another party has already made the same report or whether the affected person holds a cover that the report depends on

rules_sent_back.instruction: When the description states a check of one condition, and a second check on a different condition applies only to cases where the first check holds, with a required report or action following from the second check: Model one exclusive gateway per check, in the order the description states them. Route the branch where the first check holds by a sequence flow into the second gateway, so the second check is reached only after the first has passed. Place the required report or action as a task on the branch of the second gateway where its check holds. Do not connect the second gateway from any branch that bypasses the first check.
rules_sent_back.situation: the description states a check of one condition, and a second check on a different condition applies only to cases where the first check holds, with a required report or action following from the second check

rules_sent_back.instruction: When the description attaches a timing qualifier such as 'immediately', 'within N days' or 'in good time' to an action or to a notification sent to another party: Name the task by its action verb, its object and its addressee only, as the description states them, and leave the timing qualifier out of the task label. Record the timing as a text annotation associated with that task, so that the deadline remains visible without changing the label.
rules_sent_back.situation: the description attaches a timing qualifier such as 'immediately', 'within N days' or 'in good time' to an action or to a notification sent to another party
